title: Playing a party in the old style; banjo players
summary: A party the night before without piano reminded him of the old days; he uses banjoists Emanuel Sayles or Fred Minor.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: We were talking about the difference in music now and in the old days.
Say, now if you play a picnic today or a party or someplace off Bourbon Street, do you play like you did in the old days more or less or more like they do on Bourbon Street?

Well, let's take like for an instance last night. Well, we played a good beat all the way through. We didn't play nothing fast. We played a party last night on 4th Street for double tone party. Everybody enjoyed this stuff. We had a beat. I mean, it was a really great beat. No kidding. That reminds me of the old days. I mean, last night really reminds me of the old days. Had a pretty good band too. We didn't have no piano. We didn't use no piano last night. We had bass, banjo. Like the old time, you know? Like the old days, you know? We had no piano. And you had trouble? I had a trombone, trumpet and clarinet.
You have trouble finding a banjo now?
No, no, I don't have trouble finding a banjo. No. That's a few around. I mean.

Oh, I use, sometimes I use manual seals and most of the time I use Fred Minor. He's not the greatest but he's a pretty good boy. I mean, he plays fair, you know, fair banjo and he sings a lot of tune, you know. He's a good entertainer, you know, entertain the people. That's why, you know, I have him with me all the time. I mean, I said banjo, well I'll call Fred Minor. And he loves to work with me because he figured when I get a gig, I mean, it's always going to be, you know, pretty good. But, you know, he figured I got a lot of name, you know, and I get people to have respect for me, give me a lot of money, more money than the average guy, you know. So he figured he'd like to string along with me all the time. No, it's no problem finding a banjo player. I'm going to have quite a few of them around.
